children: The S&P Global Japan Manufacturing PMI fell to 54.1 in September from 54.9 in August, coming in slightly below market expectations of 55.0. The reading signaled the softest pace of manufacturing expansion since February, driven by slower growth in both output and new orders.

Service sector momentum also eased. The Flash Japan S&P Global Services PMI Business Activity Index dropped to 51.6 in September from August's final reading of 52.5, which had marked a five-month high.

Consequently, Japan’s S&P Global Composite PMI Business Activity Index slipped to 52.5 in September from 53.5 in August, marking its lowest level since May. The combined slowdown reflected a three-month low in factory production alongside a more modest pace of expansion in services.
